fixes.explanation: That's it. The people reply, "You have not cheated us or oppressed us…" and say he has not taken anything from the hand of man. Samuel then says the LORD and His anointed are witnesses that they have found nothing in his hand, and the people answer, "He is a witness…" So the answer is False.
Right, baker. Samuel says they asked for a king "…even though the LORD your God was your king." They already had the best King there is. So the answer is the LORD their God.

Kish isn't in this part of Samuel's speech, friend. He says they asked for a king "…even though the LORD your God was your king." Kish, Saul's father (1 Samuel 9:1, 2), doesn't come into it. The LORD is the King he names.

Yes, baker. Samuel says the LORD will not abandon His people "…because He was pleased to make you His own." It's about what He chose, not what they earned. So the answer is that He was pleased to make them His own.
